HgqjnS2N0VM.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Qalam, Part 2: Verses 8-16
HgqjnS2N0VM.one_line: The ten traits the Prophet was told not to emulate in 68:8-16, and how flipping them gives his character.
HgqjnS2N0VM.summary: After recalling that the juz is about dawah, where victory means people entering the deen rather than conquering land, he reads verses 8-16 as a list of ten traits the Prophet is told not to emulate. He first explains why the Quran often teaches by prohibition: a red line leaves wide space to act, as the shahadah itself begins with a negation. The first trait, the denier who rejects evidence he finds convincing, takes most of the session. Muslims follow evidence, build iman on the universe, history and human experience rather than on reasons for each ruling, and then trust Allah's commands the way a patient trusts a qualified doctor. Religion cannot be inherited, and a good Muslim admits error, as a Syrian Quran scholar did publicly after twenty years and as Abu Bakr did with Umar. He then covers compromise of principle (with a sharp critique of politicians' silence on Gaza), lying and lack of integrity, gossip and talebearing (he refuses to hear any), stinginess, harming others, base conduct, harshness and shame of one's own identity. Flipping all ten yields the Prophet's portrait, which the audience is asked to aspire to.

outline.heading: Recap: dawah as the goal, victory as people entering the deen
outline.gist: Last week's verse set the Prophet upon great character. The juz is about dawah, and An-Nasr defines victory as people entering Allah's religion in crowds, not conquering land, owning things or one empire beating another.

outline.heading: Our causes are about injustice, not ownership
outline.gist: Muslims keep causes central because injustice occurred and the deen requires them to stay a voice of truth; the four opening surahs give the knowledge, ethical, spiritual and behavioural requirements.

outline.heading: Let the outcomes judge whose path is right
outline.gist: Allah knows who is guided, so Muslims need not fight over it: live your values and let the results decide. Fail to live them and people will think Islam failed.

outline.heading: Do not emulate: why the Quran teaches by prohibition
outline.gist: 'La tuti'' here means do not emulate, not only do not obey. A command restricts you to a few options while a prohibition draws a red line and leaves wide space, as in the hadith to avoid what he forbids and do what he commands as much as you can.

outline.heading: The shahadah begins with a negation
outline.gist: Tawhid is stated as 'there is no god' before 'but Allah', which is why it is weighty; he tells atheists they are already halfway there.

outline.heading: Number one: the denier who rejects what he finds convincing
outline.gist: Takdhib is not plain disbelief but saying no to what makes the most sense because of arrogance, envy, fear or a lost interest, and the Quran treats it as a grave sin.

outline.heading: Muslims follow the evidence wherever it leads
outline.gist: As in 'if the Most Merciful had a son I would be the first to worship', Muslims accept truth from anyone, even people they dislike, and are never asked to walk blindly or lie to themselves.

outline.heading: Establish iman by evidence, then trust the commands
outline.gist: Certainty in Allah, the prophethood and the Quran comes through evidence; after that clear commands are followed without a reason for each, the way a patient trusts a qualified doctor without needing a medical degree.

outline.heading: Iman is built on the universe, not on the reasons for rulings
outline.gist: A clever arguer might win a debate over why something is haram, and that changes nothing. Iman is built on the universe, history and human experience, not on why there are five prayers or the Prophet's marriages; a hadith he cannot explain does not shake it.

outline.heading: You inherit your race, not your religion
outline.gist: We are Muslim because Islam makes the most sense, not because we took it from our parents; everyone must study the evidence for a Creator, his communication and his messengers themselves.

outline.heading: Converts lose nothing: Islam returns them to their own prophets
outline.gist: Islam sees other faiths as once led by great men with a book from Allah and later corrupted, so a convert gains the authentic teaching of his own prophet and belongs to his people more.

outline.heading: Stop demanding a reason for every detail
outline.gist: Children learning maths and patients questioning every drug show the flaw: trust the maxims you verified and accept what follows, or go back and fix your iman at its root.

outline.heading: A Syrian Quran master admits twenty years of error
outline.gist: A leading Syrian Quran teacher of his generation defended a disputed tajweed point, a slight lip opening in the hidden mim, for twenty years, then publicly said he had been wrong; Allah raised his name after it.

outline.heading: A challenge should send you back to your own argument
outline.gist: Defending something because it is familiar or ours is not Islamic. A challenge need not change your mind on the spot but should send you to study your own argument, as Muslims hope a Christian will re-examine the Trinity.

outline.heading: Islam never asks you to switch off your brain
outline.gist: Faith built on evidence needs logic; do not take anything on trust from anyone, even family, and write down what spouses owe each other rather than relying on trust.

outline.heading: Not because of our forefathers: Islam has the superior argument
outline.gist: Quraysh asked whether he was better than his grandfather; following forefathers is no argument. We are Muslim because Islam holds the superior argument, not the reverse, so never force things to fit.

outline.heading: The first value: adherence to the truth, and the count-and-flip method
outline.gist: He will count the traits and flip each one, since the mirror image is the Prophet. The first is adherence to truth and evidence without ego, which is why he was chosen and why those like him succeeded around him.

outline.heading: Umar and the woman who corrected him from the minbar
outline.gist: Umar, known for stopping at the Book of Allah, said a woman calling out from the back was right and he was wrong, because her point seemed stronger in that moment, even though his view held on reflection.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr rushes to admit he was wrong
outline.gist: After a quarrel with Umar, Abu Bakr came running to say the fault was his; the Prophet defended him as the one who believed in him when no one else did.

outline.heading: The first prohibition the early Muslims heard
outline.gist: These were among the first commands ever revealed, so the first thing the Quran forbade was being someone biased who will not follow the evidence.

outline.heading: Number two: they wish you would compromise
outline.gist: Idhan is giving something up for a gain. Quraysh, though stronger, kept offering deals, even asking him to seat the slaves behind the nobles, and he conceded nothing, so the stories make him sound like the one with the upper hand.

outline.heading: Politicians stand for nothing: the silence on Gaza
outline.gist: Politicians say anything for a vote, and a man like Trump is sold as a practising Christian. They stay silent on the Holy Land while children are pulled from rubble because they fear Zionist pressure and Muslims have not built enough pressure.

outline.heading: The most principled should lead; instead we pick the lesser evil
outline.gist: The leader should be the most principled person in a group, as the Prophet was. Today voters settle for the least harmful candidate, the Middle East has open dictatorship and the West a hidden one with the illusion of choice.

outline.heading: Number three: the habitual swearer, a liar for gain
outline.gist: Hallaf is a figure of speech for the liar who swears and exaggerates to escape trouble or get something out of people.

outline.heading: Number four: mahin, the one without integrity
outline.gist: Mahin has no sense of his own dignity or word and will flatter anyone or change colour to get his way.

outline.heading: Number five: the slanderer who carries tales
outline.gist: Hammaz mashsha' bi namim carries words between people to make them hate one another; tales you cannot verify only ruin relationships, so namimah is among the worst social sins.

outline.heading: His own rule: refuse to hear any gossip
outline.gist: From early in his marriage he refused all gossip, even about himself. Become boring to gossips and they stop; backbiting is eating a dead brother's flesh.

outline.heading: Rise above it: people will always talk
outline.gist: Drop gossiping friends even if it leaves you alone for a while. No one throws stones at a dead tree; those who talk about you are often envious and later seek your friendship.

outline.heading: Who has time to watch other people's lives?
outline.gist: Commenting on how others dress and behave is not the conduct of focused, purposeful people; he would buy that spare time for an eighth day of the week.

outline.heading: Number six: withholding good
outline.gist: Manna' lil-khayr withholds a kind word, money, time or help again and again, out of a selfishness that wants others to get less so he stays ahead.

outline.heading: Number seven: transgressing against others
outline.gist: Once you harm someone's space, wealth, freedom or integrity only Allah can help you; you cannot remove the pain or return stolen time, and an apology is only a first step. Arrive on the Day with clean hands.

outline.heading: Number eight: athim, conduct the community sees as low
outline.gist: Athim is one who engages in behaviour the community regards as base and unethical, below high character.

outline.heading: Number nine: 'utull, the harsh whom people abandon
outline.gist: 'Utull is the heavy, rude person others leave feeling worse; Allah told the Prophet that had he been harsh even the companions would have scattered, so family and community will not stay with someone who yells.

outline.heading: Number ten: zanim, ashamed of his own identity
outline.gist: Zanim claims a lineage, family or identity that is not his because he is ashamed of his own.

outline.heading: Count the ten, flip them, and you get Muhammad
outline.gist: The opposites are adherence to truth, steadfast principle, honesty, integrity, reconciling people, generosity, gentleness, high character, ease with people and pride in one's identity, which is exactly who the Prophet was.

outline.heading: Wealth, children and the brand on the snout
outline.gist: The one who calls the signs ancient fables because he has wealth and sons will be marked on the nose for all to see.

-vTw6595Ru0.summary: He places Al-Qalam as the second surah of Juz Tabarak, which he reads as the requirements for carrying Islam: Al-Mulk supplied knowledge, Al-Qalam supplies values and ethics. It is among the earliest revelations, and he notes how the first revealed verses, the meeting with Waraqah (whose name means paper) and a surah named the Pen all point to learning. He urges people to write and journal, since defining a value in a clear sentence is how an idea becomes a lived ethic, and he separates fixed, written values from fiqh rulings that change with time, place and person. In the verses he reads the oath by the pen as each person writing the book they will read before Allah, and as documentation driving human and Islamic civilization. He explains the denial that the Prophet is mad, the reward that is never spoiled by reminders, and the Prophet standing upon great character as a foundation, which is why he was chosen and why converts with good character excelled. The closing verses teach that time exposes values, so one need not argue or worry about those who wrong you.

outline.heading: Juz Tabarak as the requirements of carrying Islam
outline.gist: The cluster is about carrying Islam yourself and to others, since being a vehicle for guidance is a main reason to be Muslim. Its first four surahs cover knowledge, values, spirituality and behaviour; Al-Mulk gave knowledge, Al-Qalam gives values.

outline.heading: One of the very earliest revelations
outline.gist: Most scholars rank Al-Qalam second after Al-Alaq, so its phrases were the first the Muslims ever heard: its garden story was their first story and Yunus the first prophet mentioned to them.

outline.heading: The first revealed verses point to knowledge six times
outline.gist: Iqra' twice, the pen, 'allama and the verb to know: read here means reflect, contemplate and gather knowledge, not just recite a text.

outline.heading: Waraqah, whose name means paper, and a surah called the Pen
outline.gist: After the first revelation the Prophet was taken to Waraqah, who explained his whole mission; his name means paper, a seventh reference to knowledge, and the next surah revealed is named the Pen.

outline.heading: Writing is how things sink in: the Libyan memorizers
outline.gist: Typing does not stick but writing does; Libyan and Somali students memorize the Quran by writing it and win the big competitions, and concepts sink in the same way.

outline.heading: Structure a sentence to build a value
outline.gist: He asks people to stop the reels and journal: a word like honesty is abstract until you define it in a sentence, and structuring that sentence is half the work of building an ethic.

outline.heading: The Quran preserved because it was written
outline.gist: Over a thousand companions memorized it, but it reaches us down to every articulation because it was written from day one, on bones, wood and palm leaves when writing material was hard to find.

outline.heading: Defining honesty: a worked example
outline.gist: A notebook will not ruin the Amazon. Honesty means telling the truth when it is uncomfortable or costly, without being rude or blunt about people's feelings.

outline.heading: Values are written: the pens have been lifted
outline.gist: The pen symbolises that values are documented and fixed, as the Prophet said of decree that the pens are lifted and the pages dry.

outline.heading: Fiqh is dynamic, values are fixed
outline.gist: Rulings respond to time, place, person and circumstance, so a new Muslim's fiqh differs from a lifelong Muslim's; honesty, trust, loyalty, kindness and empathy are the same in any century.

outline.heading: Take rulings locally; differ on fiqh, never on values
outline.gist: This surah has almost no fiqh. Ask your local scholar rather than a sheikh in another country; scholars differ on wiping over socks by design, but no sheikh differs on honesty or justice.

outline.heading: A surah every Muslim needs
outline.gist: If he had to choose one surah for people to hear, it would be this one: its values speak equally to the imam, the lifelong Muslim and the new Muslim.

outline.heading: Nun: its recitation and the challenge theory
outline.gist: Nun takes six counts. The most accepted view of the opening letters is that they challenged the Arab poets with their own letters.

outline.heading: The opening letters as coding: a fourth dimension
outline.gist: Surahs sharing the same opening letters share a common thread. Beyond when a surah was revealed, where it sits, and what it does for you, the letters add a fourth dimension we do not yet fully grasp.

outline.heading: Allah's oaths carry content and need an answer
outline.gist: Allah never swears aimlessly: what he swears by tells a story before the answer comes, unlike our oaths by Allah or the Prophet's oath by the One in whose hand is his soul.

outline.heading: The oath by the pen: you are writing your own book
outline.gist: Every choice writes the novel you will read aloud before Allah, perhaps with others listening, with your motives and thoughts laid bare, so choose the story you want to read.

outline.heading: Documentation let humanity build on itself
outline.gist: Written history is scarce until the last millennium or so; once knowledge was recorded, people could absorb a whole civilization's rise and fall in hours and build on it.

outline.heading: Muslims led the boom of documentation
outline.gist: Muslims translated and extended Greek, Persian and Roman learning, Aristotle included, instead of burning it. Writing preserved the Quran exactly and saved the hadith, and narrators who lost their written records were not relied on.

outline.heading: Two readings of 'you are not mad'
outline.gist: The answer to the oath: either by your Lord's grace you are not mad, or, as he prefers, in spreading your Lord's blessing, the Quran, you are not mad.

outline.heading: Called mad, never a liar: forty years without a lie
outline.gist: Madness was the first accusation because Quraysh could not call him a liar after forty years in which no one close to him heard a lie, a rare thing that takes a certain personality.

outline.heading: Ghayr mamnun: a reward never spoiled by reminders
outline.gist: A gift repeatedly brought up becomes a burden, as the Quran warns against spoiling charity with reminders; the reward is free of being told you did not deserve it.

outline.heading: Allah makes you feel you earned it
outline.gist: The Quran attends to the psychological side of reward: whoever enters Paradise knowing it is Allah's bounty is made to feel he earned it, so the joy is complete, which one-word translations like 'unending' miss.

outline.heading: Values and ethics: the ethic is the value made visible
outline.gist: The answer to the oath has three parts, the third being 'upon great character'. A value such as empathy is one word; the ethic is how it shows up with each person, though some philosophers split them as individual versus community.

outline.heading: 'Ala: ethics as the ground you stand on
outline.gist: The Arabs pictured ethics as a foundation you stand upon, letting you hold your head high, see further and not lose your footing.

outline.heading: Chosen for his character; people are like minerals
outline.gist: He had great character before prophethood, and that is why he was chosen. The best of people before Islam are the best in Islam once they learn it.

outline.heading: Umar and Hamza: late converts who excelled through their values
outline.gist: Umar came six years late yet became central to the religion, and the seerah books give his and Hamza's conversions their own chapter, because their values were ready; those who lied and cheated take far longer to change.

EC9O6DzHJqU.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The Third Article, Reforming Social Values (Part 2)
EC9O6DzHJqU.one_line: Every society has values: reinforce the good ones, push back on the bad, keep this distinct from dawah, and see how the Prophet reformed Arab values.
EC9O6DzHJqU.summary: His second khutbah on the third article of the Aqabah pledge, the Prophet's condition that Madinah accept a reform of its social values. He grounds the article in 'urf, custom, which jurists use as a secondary source of evidence, and in the word ma'ruf, the known good. Every society has values; Muslims should neither pretend otherwise nor try to erase them, but identify what they share, reinforce it in practice, and push back against the rest. He separates this from dawah: calling someone to Islam needs preparation, a relationship and finesse aimed at making them love Allah, while asking someone not to take a handicap spot needs only conviction, and mixing the two loses both. Al-Hajj 22:41 pairs ritual with reformed values. Values abandoned through silence are lost, which he says the confusion around gender shows, and Muslims, Arabs especially, are themselves known for rudeness and disregard for others. The Prophet kept the Arabs' generosity and loyalty but ended racism, female infanticide, usury and autocracy, beginning by consulting people himself. In the second khutbah he cites the warning that abandoning enjoining good brings punishment and unanswered dua, and laments the crime, abuse and dishonesty he sees in the community.

outline.heading: Opening
Returning to the third article: the status quo will not be accepted
outline.gist: Muslims misunderstand this concept and mix it with other things. The Prophet made it a condition of coming to Madinah: some values he would strengthen, explain and praise, others he would push against and remove; he was not coming to validate all of their values.

outline.heading: 'Urf: custom as a source of evidence
outline.gist: Beyond the four agreed sources, Quran, Sunnah, consensus and analogy, scholars use other sources when those are silent, and custom is one of them. The word ma'ruf literally means simply "that which is known".

outline.heading: Ma'ruf: the known good
outline.gist: Being an optimistic desert people, the Arabs used the bare word to mean what is known to be good and beneficial. So ma'ruf is about the norms of your society: the values you agree with you reinforce through behaviour, practice and reminders, and the ones you do not you push back against.

outline.heading: Every society has values
outline.gist: It is arrogant to imagine any people has no values: some write them into a constitution, others simply live them and you notice them over time. Muslims do not ask anyone to erase everything they have and take a new set.

outline.heading: Values work is not dawah
outline.gist: Rituals and acts of worship matter, but bringing people to them is dawah, which has its own art. The distinction exists because once you mix the two, one or both get lost.

outline.heading: Inviting to Islam versus asking him not to block a driveway
outline.gist: Calling a non-Muslim to Islam and asking the same man not to take a handicap spot or block a driveway are different acts done by different people. Not everyone is qualified for dawah: it needs preparation, education, a relationship, the right circumstances and finesse.

outline.heading: The goal of dawah is that they love Allah
outline.gist: The art of dawah is bringing people closer to Allah so they love Him. If you do not know how to do that, be a facilitator and bring someone who does; everyone has a role, but not necessarily the speaking role.

outline.heading: Values need only conviction
outline.gist: Upholding values needs no finesse or preparation: reinforce the ones we share, call out those who break them, and push back on the rest vocally, through advocacy, politics and the media. Both are fully required in the deen, and dawah is the fourth article.

outline.heading: Ritual and values together
outline.gist: In Al-Hajj 22:41 those given authority in the land establish prayer and zakat and command good and forbid wrong: both must happen. Luqman's advice to his son makes everyone responsible for values, though not everyone should be giving religious advice.

outline.heading: Fewer fatwas, more basic decency
outline.gist: Stop passing on a shaykh's opinion as the only one when it is one among many acceptable views. Values are clear: respect, empathy, equality, kindness, standing in line, leaving your car where it blocks no one, the basics of human decency.

outline.heading: Stop fighting for a value and you lose it
outline.gist: In one area of life the basics are already gone: people fear being fired over pronouns and no longer know how to define male and female or who may marry. Stop pointing things out and you lose them, so say plainly that no one may speak to or treat a child, a wife, a client or any human being that way.

outline.heading: Etiquette is itself a value
outline.gist: This is not a call to aggression: speaking to people in the best way is one of our values. Instead Muslims, Arabs especially, are known as rough and loud and as not respecting other people's space.

outline.heading: 'Me first, let the flood take everyone'
outline.gist: The attitude that only my getting through matters is not Islamic. Children must not grow up thinking they can bully others or answer elders disrespectfully; dawah and values overlap, but the Prophet and the Quran distinguished them.

outline.heading: Values are shared by humanity
outline.gist: No one needs to be Muslim to agree that people are equal and deserve the same rights and respect, which is why this is not dawah. When people lose their values they lose everything; the Arabs were generous and kept their word but were deeply racist.

outline.heading: What the Prophet ended
outline.gist: Racism, worse then than in today's worst gatherings, burying newborn daughters, a distorted view of women and usury were values he declared done with. Governance was another: everyone was to have a voice.

outline.heading: Ending one-man rule, starting with himself
outline.gist: Arabs sat before their chief and flattered him; no one's opinion mattered. The Prophet, who had revelation, began asking people what to do, because the Quran told him to consult them, and the change of value started with himself.

outline.heading: Our task: name the values and practise them first
outline.gist: Muslims in this country must identify the values here that are Islamic, be first to practise and teach them, and push back on the rest vocally, appropriately and with sound arguments. It is complicated, and only small silos of Muslims are thinking about it.

outline.heading: Those who clung to the old values lost their status
outline.gist: The Ansar understood that things would change: anyone who kept up tribal hostility, usury or drinking lost his standing. Here our basic values are threatened, and we must acknowledge it before we can change our reality.

outline.heading: Interlude
After Badr: wealth with a right for others
outline.gist: A change of value beyond zakat: wealth that comes in is not only for those who took part but strengthens the poor. The companions disliked it and said what they should not have, revelation told them not to quarrel over it, and they later admitted their conduct.

outline.heading: Command good, or your dua goes unanswered
outline.gist: In an authentic narration the Prophet swore that you will command good and forbid wrong, or Allah will soon send a punishment and then not answer you when you call on Him. Once values rot, what is the point?

outline.heading: White clothes, black heart: the dusty traveller
outline.gist: Praying in the first row dressed in white means nothing if the heart is black. The dishevelled traveller raises his hands to Allah while his food and drink are haram; values decide whether you touch haram when you are hungry or in need.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr corrects the reading of 5:105
outline.gist: Refusing haram in a financial pinch while fearing for your children is a value. Abu Bakr on the minbar told people they recite "you are responsible for yourselves" without understanding it, for he heard the Prophet say that if they do not command good and forbid wrong, Allah will punish them all.

outline.heading: Our community's failing values
outline.gist: Our basic values are being questioned and we are not upholding them: in his work with people he sees crime, domestic abuse, corners cut, untrustworthy dealings and disregard for law and order.

outline.heading: How can we ask for victory?
outline.gist: We keep asking Allah for success and victory while we cannot uphold basic decency, respect or empathy among ourselves. It has changed many times before and will change through people who care, but pretending all is well leaves our children questioning their values.

outline.heading: Outro

6:53.en: And thus We have tried some of them through others that the disbelievers might say, "Is it these whom Allah has favored among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful

47:38.ar: هَٰٓأَنتُمۡ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ تُدۡعَوۡنَ لِتُنفِقُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَمِنكُم مَّن يَبۡخَلُۖ وَمَن يَبۡخَلۡ فَإِنَّمَا يَبۡخَلُ عَن نَّفۡسِهِۦۚ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ وَأَنتُمُ ٱلۡفُقَرَآءُۚ وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوۡاْ يَسۡتَبۡدِلۡ قَوۡمًا غَيۡرَكُمۡ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُونُوٓاْ أَمۡثَٰلَكُم
47:38.en: Here you are - those invited to spend in the cause of Allah - but among you are those who withhold [out of greed]. And whoever withholds only withholds [benefit] from himself; and Allah is the Free of need, while you are the needy. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be the likes of you

6:162.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحۡيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
6:162.en: Say, "Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds

19:59.ar: ۞فَخَلَفَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ خَلۡفٌ أَضَاعُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ ٱلشَّهَوَٰتِۖ فَسَوۡفَ يَلۡقَوۡنَ غَيًّا
19:59.en: But there came after them successors who neglected prayer and pursued desires; so they are going to meet evil

7:169.ar: فَخَلَفَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ خَلۡفࣱ وَرِثُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ يَأۡخُذُونَ عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلۡأَدۡنَىٰ وَيَقُولُونَ سَيُغۡفَرُ لَنَا وَإِن يَأۡتِهِمۡ عَرَضࣱ مِّثۡلُهُۥ يَأۡخُذُوهُۚ أَلَمۡ يُؤۡخَذۡ عَلَيۡهِم مِّيثَٰقُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ أَن لَّا يَقُولُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡحَقَّ وَدَرَسُواْ مَا فِيهِۗ وَٱلدَّارُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ خَيۡرࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
7:169.en: And there followed them successors who inherited the Scripture [while] taking the commodities of this lower life and saying, "It will be forgiven for us." And if an offer like it comes to them, they will [again] take it. Was not the covenant of the Scripture taken from them that they would not say about Allah except the truth, and they studied what was in it? And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, so will you not use reason

aCbF16D8RYw.speaker: adnan
aCbF16D8RYw.speaker_note: Seventh khutbah of his own Pledge of Al-Aqabah series; same voice, structure and Arabic second khutbah as the earlier episodes.
aCbF16D8RYw.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The Fourth Article, Prioritizing the Message
aCbF16D8RYw.one_line: The fourth article of the Aqabah pledge: put Allah's message above everything, refuse compromise, and stand for Allah without fearing anyone's blame.
aCbF16D8RYw.summary: His seventh khutbah on the Pledge of Al-Aqabah takes the article in which the Ansar promised to stand up for Allah without fearing anyone's blame. He opens with Al-Ma'idah 5:54: if people turn away, Allah brings a people He loves, who love Him and do not fear the critic. Yathrib, he says, was a city with no future, torn by tribal hatred and poverty, and the Prophet came to it only once its people offered the pledge; if you want him to do for your life what he did for that city, the same commitment is required. The key is priority. Islam is the umbrella over life, not one category competing with others, and Al-Hujurat 49:1 forbids putting anything ahead of Allah and His Messenger. He asks how anyone will explain a life of 'I was too busy' to God, reads As-Saff 61:10-11 as a transaction of self and wealth, and recalls how Quraysh pressed for a small compromise to strip the message of its authenticity. In the Arabic second khutbah he says this dedication needs courage and is driven by love of Allah, built by recalling His gifts and patience. He then holds up Gaza as a test of what we really put first, and warns from Maryam 19:59 and Al-A'raf 7:169 about generations who let the message slip.

outline.heading: Opening
The people Allah loves
outline.gist: Al-Ma'idah 5:54 frames the article: if any of you turn back from the deen, Allah will bring a people He loves and who love Him, humble with believers, firm against disbelievers, striving in His way and fearing no critic's blame. He turns to the Ansar who came to Aqabah.

outline.heading: From Yathrib to the city everyone longs for
outline.gist: Madinah is now the city people around the globe would do anything to visit, where you find nothing but peace, calm and beauty. The Prophet made it that, and he went there only once its people offered him the pledge.

outline.heading: Do for your life what he did for Yathrib
outline.gist: If you want the Prophet to come into your life and do for it what he did for Yathrib, the same pledge is required. Yathrib, a name that means little to us now, was broken from the inside: its people hated each other, it was filled with poverty and its tribes fought year after year.

outline.heading: Sent to the city with no future
outline.gist: Of his many attempts to present himself to the tribes, 26 are on record, and some he did not bother to approach because he knew them. Allah sent him to a place that was not functioning, had no future and was only getting worse, so that you could see what the message does.

outline.heading: The articles of the pledge
outline.gist: He lists them: hearing and obeying in energy and reluctance, spending in hardship and ease, commanding good and forbidding wrong, and today's article, standing for Allah without fearing the blame of any critic.

outline.heading: 'Turns back': more than apostasy
outline.gist: The fourth article is staying steadfast on priority even when people criticize you for it. The verb for turning back in 5:54 is used in jurisprudence for apostasy, but it covers any lack of priority for the deen.

outline.heading: Fearless because their priority is right
outline.gist: The people Allah brings will not fear isolation or the haters' blame, because they know their priorities: Islam is the umbrella for life and everything else falls under it.

outline.heading: Islam is not a category: nothing ahead of Allah
outline.gist: Islam is not one category of life competing with others for a share of your time. Al-Hujurat 49:1 forbids putting anything at all ahead of Allah and His Messenger.

outline.heading: Why are we alive?
outline.gist: Why do I have consciousness, the ability to think deeply, make complex choices and know innately what is right and good? No other creature on the planet runs into ethical dilemmas.

outline.heading: Only one answer, and a life to explain
outline.gist: No animal lies depressed wondering whether it should have chosen differently, yet I do. There is only one answer to who put me here, and once you have it, the question is how you will explain your life and justify your choices before Allah.

outline.heading: 'I was too busy': make the argument
outline.gist: He invites anyone with a better argument to convince him how a person could tell God "I didn't have enough time, I was too busy", and make it logical. As-Saff 61:10 offers a transaction that saves from a painful punishment.

outline.heading: The transaction: wealth and self
outline.gist: Believing in Allah and His Messenger and striving with your wealth and yourselves means giving what you own inside and outside for Allah; anything less does not fulfil the purpose. That is the full commitment and priority the Prophet asked for, with no compromise.

outline.heading: Quraysh's small compromise
outline.gist: In the sixth to eighth years of his prophethood Quraysh tried to negotiate a small compromise. People who stand for nothing want you to compromise a little because it strips the halo of authenticity, originality and divinity from your faith, and he never conceded.

outline.heading: Do not drive away the weak believers
outline.gist: Al-An'am 6:52-53: do not drive away those who call on their Lord morning and evening seeking His face. The elite were tested by them, asking how Allah could favour such people over them; does Allah not know best who is grateful?

outline.heading: Take it in its totality
outline.gist: You take every aspect of the message, even where you cannot yet do all of it, commit your whole life to it and make every choice aim at getting you across the finishing line.

outline.heading: Anything less than your whole life falls short (Arabic)
outline.gist: The Prophet asked the Ansar that night to stand for Allah: devotion and sincerity, giving your life to the One who gave it. Anything less than our whole life and wealth is a real shortcoming, and Muhammad 47:38 warns that Allah can replace us with a people not like us.

outline.heading: Fearing no blame takes courage, and love
outline.gist: Do not fear anyone asking why you did it, calling it shameful or accusing you of dividing people. That needs courage, devotion, a firm hold on guidance and above all love, since no one devotes himself to someone he does not love; love of Allah is the first and last driver of this deen.

outline.heading: Recalling how patient He has been
outline.gist: Love Him by recalling how much He gave and guided you and how forbearing He was while you disobeyed and turned from His command, never expelling you from His door. Offering Him less than yourself and your wealth would be ugly character; say, as in Al-An'am 6:162, my prayer, sacrifice, life and death are for Allah.

outline.heading: Should I not be a grateful servant?
outline.gist: The Prophet stood in prayer until his feet swelled and said "should I not be a grateful servant?", and Aisha asked who could bear what he bore. The message cannot be number two in our lives.

outline.heading: Gaza: how many more children?
outline.gist: How can a billion and more Muslims not put this in its proper place of priority? How many more months, how many more children have to die, and how can anyone with a child he loves think about anything else?

outline.heading: Generations who let the message slip
outline.gist: Maryam 19:59 and Al-A'raf 7:169: successors who wasted prayer and followed desires, who inherited the Book and took the goods of this world saying "we will be forgiven". Without the priority, we will not find the beauty, ease and joy the Prophet's people found.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Priorities: putting Allah and His message first
themes.note: Islam is the umbrella over life, not a category competing with others; nothing may be placed ahead of Allah and His Messenger, and the message is taken in its totality without compromise.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: Yathrib before the Prophet was a city with no future; he reached it after many attempts with the tribes and only once its people offered the pledge.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: Quraysh's negotiations sought a small compromise to empty the message of its authenticity, and their leaders asked him to dismiss the weak believers; he refused both.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Human consciousness and moral struggle point to one answer about who put us here, and that answer demands a life you can justify before God.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: 'I was too busy' and 'I didn't have enough time' are not arguments anyone can make to God.

themes.label: Courage and commitment: going all in
themes.note: Standing for Allah while people ask why you did it, call it shameful or accuse you of causing division takes courage, dedication and a firm hold on guidance.

themes.label: Love: of Allah, the Prophet, and one another
themes.note: No one dedicates himself to anyone he does not love; love of Allah is the first and last driver of the deen, built by recalling His gifts and forbearance.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: The continuing killing of children in Gaza is held up as the test of whether the ummah's priorities are right.

takeaways: Treat Islam as the umbrella over your whole life rather than one compartment competing with work, family and leisure
Check decisions against Al-Hujurat 49:1: nothing goes ahead of Allah and His Messenger

28:2.en: These are the verses of the clear Book

28:3.ar: نَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡكَ مِن نَّبَإِ مُوسَىٰ وَفِرۡعَوۡنَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ لِقَوۡمࣲ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
28:3.en: We recite to you from the news of Moses and Pharaoh in truth for a people who believe

28:4.ar: إِنَّ فِرۡعَوۡنَ عَلَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَجَعَلَ أَهۡلَهَا شِيَعࣰ ا يَسۡتَضۡعِفُ طَآئِفَةࣰ مِّنۡهُمۡ يُذَبِّحُ أَبۡنَآءَهُمۡ وَيَسۡتَحۡيِۦ نِسَآءَهُمۡۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
28:4.en: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people into factions, oppressing a sector among them, slaughtering their [newborn] sons and keeping their females alive. Indeed, he was of the corrupters

28:5.ar: وَنُرِيدُ أَن نَّمُنَّ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَنَجۡعَلَهُمۡ أَئِمَّةࣰ وَنَجۡعَلَهُمُ ٱلۡوَٰرِثِينَ
28:5.en: And We wanted to confer favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them inheritors

28:6.ar: وَنُمَكِّنَ لَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَنُرِيَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا مِنۡهُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَحۡذَرُونَ
28:6.en: And establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and [his minister] Haman and their soldiers through them that which they had feared

28:7.ar: وَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنۡ أَرۡضِعِيهِۖ فَإِذَا خِفۡتِ عَلَيۡهِ فَأَلۡقِيهِ فِي ٱلۡيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِي وَلَا تَحۡزَنِيٓۖ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيۡكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ
28:7.en: And We inspired to the mother of Moses, "Suckle him; but when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him [one] of the messengers

28:8.ar: فَٱلۡتَقَطَهُۥٓ ءَالُ فِرۡعَوۡنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمۡ عَدُوࣰّ ا وَحَزَنًاۗ إِنَّ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا كَانُواْ خَٰطِـِٔينَ
28:8.en: And the family of Pharaoh picked him up [out of the river] so that he would become to them an enemy and a [cause of] grief. Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers were deliberate sinners

28:9.ar: وَقَالَتِ ٱمۡرَأَتُ فِرۡعَوۡنَ قُرَّتُ عَيۡنࣲ لِّي وَلَكَۖ لَا تَقۡتُلُوهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوۡ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدࣰ ا وَهُمۡ لَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
28:9.en: And the wife of Pharaoh said, "[He will be] a comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son." And they perceived not

28:10.ar: وَأَصۡبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَٰرِغًاۖ إِن كَادَتۡ لَتُبۡدِي بِهِۦ لَوۡلَآ أَن رَّبَطۡنَا عَلَىٰ قَلۡبِهَا لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
28:10.en: And the heart of Moses' mother became empty [of all else]. She was about to disclose [the matter concerning] him had We not bound fast her heart that she would be of the believers

28:11.ar: وَقَالَتۡ لِأُخۡتِهِۦ قُصِّيهِۖ فَبَصُرَتۡ بِهِۦ عَن جُنُبࣲ وَهُمۡ لَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
28:11.en: And she said to his sister, "Follow him"; so she watched him from a distance while they perceived not

28:12.ar: ۞وَحَرَّمۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَرَاضِعَ مِن قَبۡلُ فَقَالَتۡ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِ بَيۡتࣲ يَكۡفُلُونَهُۥ لَكُمۡ وَهُمۡ لَهُۥ نَٰصِحُونَ
28:12.en: And We had prevented from him [all] wet nurses before, so she said, "Shall I direct you to a household that will be responsible for him for you while they are to him [for his upbringing] sincere

28:13.ar: فَرَدَدۡنَٰهُ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّهِۦ كَيۡ تَقَرَّ عَيۡنُهَا وَلَا تَحۡزَنَ وَلِتَعۡلَمَ أَنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
28:13.en: So We restored him to his mother that she might be content and not grieve and that she would know that the promise of Allah is true. But most of the people do not know

28:14.ar: وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَٱسۡتَوَىٰٓ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ حُكۡمࣰ ا وَعِلۡمࣰ اۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
28:14.en: And when he attained his full strength and was [mentally] mature, We bestowed upon him judgement and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good

28:15.ar: وَدَخَلَ ٱلۡمَدِينَةَ عَلَىٰ حِينِ غَفۡلَةࣲ مِّنۡ أَهۡلِهَا فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيۡنِ يَقۡتَتِلَانِ هَٰذَا مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ وَهَٰذَا مِنۡ عَدُوِّهِۦۖ فَٱسۡتَغَٰثَهُ ٱلَّذِي مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ عَلَى ٱلَّذِي مِنۡ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَوَكَزَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيۡهِۖ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِنۡ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَدُوࣱّ مُّضِلࣱّ مُّبِينࣱ‏
28:15.en: And he entered the city at a time of inattention by its people and found therein two men fighting: one from his faction and one from among his enemy. And the one from his faction called for help to him against the one from his enemy, so Moses struck him and [unintentionally] killed him. [Moses] said, "This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is a manifest, misleading enemy

28:16.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي ظَلَمۡتُ نَفۡسِي فَٱغۡفِرۡ لِي فَغَفَرَ لَهُۥٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
28:16.en: He said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me," and He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful

28:17.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ بِمَآ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيَّ فَلَنۡ أَكُونَ ظَهِيرࣰ ا لِّلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ
28:17.en: He said, "My Lord, for the favor You bestowed upon me, I will never be an assistant to the criminals

28:18.ar: فَأَصۡبَحَ فِي ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ خَآئِفࣰ ا يَتَرَقَّبُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِي ٱسۡتَنصَرَهُۥ بِٱلۡأَمۡسِ يَسۡتَصۡرِخُهُۥۚ قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّكَ لَغَوِيࣱّ مُّبِينࣱ‏
28:18.en: And he became inside the city fearful and anticipating [exposure], when suddenly the one who sought his help the previous day cried out to him [once again]. Moses said to him, "Indeed, you are an evident, [persistent] deviator

28:19.ar: فَلَمَّآ أَنۡ أَرَادَ أَن يَبۡطِشَ بِٱلَّذِي هُوَ عَدُوࣱّ لَّهُمَا قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَتُرِيدُ أَن تَقۡتُلَنِي كَمَا قَتَلۡتَ نَفۡسَۢا بِٱلۡأَمۡسِۖ إِن تُرِيدُ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ جَبَّارࣰ ا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا تُرِيدُ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُصۡلِحِينَ
28:19.en: And when he wanted to strike the one who was an enemy to both of them, he said, "O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed someone yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land and do not want to be of the amenders

28:20.ar: وَجَآءَ رَجُلࣱ مِّنۡ أَقۡصَا ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ يَسۡعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱلۡمَلَأَ يَأۡتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقۡتُلُوكَ فَٱخۡرُجۡ إِنِّي لَكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ
28:20.en: And a man came from the farthest end of the city, running. He said, "O Moses, indeed the eminent ones are conferring over you [intending] to kill you, so leave [the city]; indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisors

28:21.ar: فَخَرَجَ مِنۡهَا خَآئِفࣰ ا يَتَرَقَّبُۖ قَالَ رَبِّ نَجِّنِي مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
28:21.en: So he left it, fearful and anticipating [apprehension]. He said, "My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people

28:22.ar: وَلَمَّا تَوَجَّهَ تِلۡقَآءَ مَدۡيَنَ قَالَ عَسَىٰ رَبِّيٓ أَن يَهۡدِيَنِي سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
28:22.en: And when he directed himself toward Madyan, he said, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the sound way

28:23.ar: وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَآءَ مَدۡيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيۡهِ أُمَّةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ يَسۡقُونَ وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمۡرَأَتَيۡنِ تَذُودَانِۖ قَالَ مَا خَطۡبُكُمَاۖ قَالَتَا لَا نَسۡقِي حَتَّىٰ يُصۡدِرَ ٱلرِّعَآءُۖ وَأَبُونَا شَيۡخࣱ كَبِيرࣱ‏
28:23.en: And when he came to the well of Madyan, he found there a crowd of people watering [their flocks], and he found aside from them two women driving back [their flocks]. He said, "What is your circumstance?" They said, "We do not water until the shepherds dispatch [their flocks]; and our father is an old man

28:24.ar: فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لِمَآ أَنزَلۡتَ إِلَيَّ مِنۡ خَيۡرࣲ فَقِيرࣱ‏
28:24.en: So he watered [their flocks] for them; then he went back to the shade and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need

28:25.ar: فَجَآءَتۡهُ إِحۡدَىٰهُمَا تَمۡشِي عَلَى ٱسۡتِحۡيَآءࣲ قَالَتۡ إِنَّ أَبِي يَدۡعُوكَ لِيَجۡزِيَكَ أَجۡرَ مَا سَقَيۡتَ لَنَاۚ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُۥ وَقَصَّ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡقَصَصَ قَالَ لَا تَخَفۡۖ نَجَوۡتَ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
28:25.en: Then one of the two women came to him walking with shyness. She said, "Indeed, my father invites you that he may reward you for having watered for us." So when he came to him and related to him the story, he said, "Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people

28:26.ar: قَالَتۡ إِحۡدَىٰهُمَا يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱسۡتَـٔۡجِرۡهُۖ إِنَّ خَيۡرَ مَنِ ٱسۡتَـٔۡجَرۡتَ ٱلۡقَوِيُّ ٱلۡأَمِينُ
28:26.en: One of the women said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy

28:27.ar: قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أُرِيدُ أَنۡ أُنكِحَكَ إِحۡدَى ٱبۡنَتَيَّ هَٰتَيۡنِ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَأۡجُرَنِي ثَمَٰنِيَ حِجَجࣲۖ فَإِنۡ أَتۡمَمۡتَ عَشۡرࣰ ا فَمِنۡ عِندِكَۖ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنۡ أَشُقَّ عَلَيۡكَۚ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
28:27.en: He said, "Indeed, I wish to wed you one of these, my two daughters, on [the condition] that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it will be [as a favor] from you. And I do not wish to put you in difficulty. You will find me, if Allah wills, from among the righteous

28:28.ar: قَالَ ذَٰلِكَ بَيۡنِي وَبَيۡنَكَۖ أَيَّمَا ٱلۡأَجَلَيۡنِ قَضَيۡتُ فَلَا عُدۡوَٰنَ عَلَيَّۖ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلࣱ‏
28:28.en: [Moses] said, "That is [established] between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I complete - there is no injustice to me, and Allah, over what we say, is Witness

28:29.ar: ۞فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلۡأَجَلَ وَسَارَ بِأَهۡلِهِۦٓ ءَانَسَ مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ نَارࣰ اۖ قَالَ لِأَهۡلِهِ ٱمۡكُثُوٓاْ إِنِّيٓ ءَانَسۡتُ نَارࣰ ا لَّعَلِّيٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنۡهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوۡ جَذۡوَةࣲ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَصۡطَلُونَ
28:29.en: And when Moses had completed the term and was traveling with his family, he perceived from the direction of the mount a fire. He said to his family, "Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I will bring you from there [some] information or burning wood from the fire that you may warm yourselves

28:30.ar: فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِيَ مِن شَٰطِيِٕ ٱلۡوَادِ ٱلۡأَيۡمَنِ فِي ٱلۡبُقۡعَةِ ٱلۡمُبَٰرَكَةِ مِنَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ أَن يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنِّيٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
28:30.en: But when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley in a blessed spot - from the tree, "O Moses, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds

28:31.ar: وَأَنۡ أَلۡقِ عَصَاكَۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهۡتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنࣱّ وَلَّىٰ مُدۡبِرࣰ ا وَلَمۡ يُعَقِّبۡۚ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَقۡبِلۡ وَلَا تَخَفۡۖ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلۡأٓمِنِينَ
28:31.en: And [he was told], "Throw down your staff." But when he saw it writhing as if it was a snake, he turned in flight and did not return. [Allah said], "O Moses, approach and fear not. Indeed, you are of the secure

28:32.ar: ٱسۡلُكۡ يَدَكَ فِي جَيۡبِكَ تَخۡرُجۡ بَيۡضَآءَ مِنۡ غَيۡرِ سُوٓءࣲ وَٱضۡمُمۡ إِلَيۡكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ ٱلرَّهۡبِۖ فَذَٰنِكَ بُرۡهَٰنَانِ مِن رَّبِّكَ إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَمَلَإِيْهِۦٓۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ قَوۡمࣰ ا فَٰسِقِينَ
28:32.en: Insert your hand into the opening of your garment; it will come out white, without disease. And draw in your arm close to you [as prevention] from fear, for those are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his establishment. Indeed, they have been a people defiantly disobedient

28:33.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي قَتَلۡتُ مِنۡهُمۡ نَفۡسࣰ ا فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقۡتُلُونِ
28:33.en: He said, "My Lord, indeed, I killed from among them someone, and I fear they will kill me

28:34.ar: وَأَخِي هَٰرُونُ هُوَ أَفۡصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانࣰ ا فَأَرۡسِلۡهُ مَعِيَ رِدۡءࣰ ا يُصَدِّقُنِيٓۖ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
28:34.en: And my brother Aaron is more fluent than me in tongue, so send him with me as support, verifying me. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me

28:35.ar: قَالَ سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ وَنَجۡعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلۡطَٰنࣰ ا فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيۡكُمَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآۚ أَنتُمَا وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكُمَا ٱلۡغَٰلِبُونَ
28:35.en: [Allah] said, "We will strengthen your arm through your brother and grant you both supremacy so they will not reach you. [It will be] through Our signs; you and those who follow you will be the predominant

28:36.ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم مُّوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا بَيِّنَٰتࣲ قَالُواْ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحۡرࣱ مُّفۡتَرࣰ ى وَمَا سَمِعۡنَا بِهَٰذَا فِيٓ ءَابَآئِنَا ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
28:36.en: But when Moses came to them with Our signs as clear evidences, they said, "This is not except invented magic, and we have not heard of this [religion] among our forefathers

28:37.ar: وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ رَبِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَن جَآءَ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ مِنۡ عِندِهِۦ وَمَن تَكُونُ لَهُۥ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلدَّارِۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفۡلِحُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
28:37.en: And Moses said, "My Lord is more knowing [than we or you] of who has come with guidance from Him and to whom will be succession in the home. Indeed, wrongdoers do not succeed

28:38.ar: وَقَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنُ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡمَلَأُ مَا عَلِمۡتُ لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرِي فَأَوۡقِدۡ لِي يَٰهَٰمَٰنُ عَلَى ٱلطِّينِ فَٱجۡعَل لِّي صَرۡحࣰ ا لَّعَلِّيٓ أَطَّلِعُ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّهُۥ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰذِبِينَ
28:38.en: And Pharaoh said, "O eminent ones, I have not known you to have a god other than me. Then ignite for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay and make for me a tower that I may look at the God of Moses. And indeed, I do think he is among the liars

28:39.ar: وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ هُوَ وَجُنُودُهُۥ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُمۡ إِلَيۡنَا لَا يُرۡجَعُونَ
28:39.en: And he was arrogant, he and his soldiers, in the land, without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us

28:40.ar: فَأَخَذۡنَٰهُ وَجُنُودَهُۥ فَنَبَذۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡيَمِّۖ فَٱنظُرۡ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
28:40.en: So We took him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea. So see how was the end of the wrongdoers

28:41.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَٰهُمۡ أَئِمَّةࣰ يَدۡعُونَ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِۖ وَيَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ لَا يُنصَرُونَ
28:41.en: And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped

28:42.ar: وَأَتۡبَعۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لَعۡنَةࣰۖ وَيَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ هُم مِّنَ ٱلۡمَقۡبُوحِينَ
28:42.en: And We caused to overtake them in this world a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be of the despised

28:43.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَآ أَهۡلَكۡنَا ٱلۡقُرُونَ ٱلۡأُولَىٰ بَصَآئِرَ لِلنَّاسِ وَهُدࣰ ى وَرَحۡمَةࣰ لَّعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
28:43.en: And We gave Moses the Scripture, after We had destroyed the former generations, as enlightenment for the people and guidance and mercy that they might be reminded

28:44.ar: وَمَا كُنتَ بِجَانِبِ ٱلۡغَرۡبِيِّ إِذۡ قَضَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلۡأَمۡرَ وَمَا كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
28:44.en: And you, [O Muhammad], were not on the western side [of the mount] when We revealed to Moses the command, and you were not among the witnesses [to that]

28:45.ar: وَلَٰكِنَّآ أَنشَأۡنَا قُرُونࣰ ا فَتَطَاوَلَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡعُمُرُۚ وَمَا كُنتَ ثَاوِيࣰ ا فِيٓ أَهۡلِ مَدۡيَنَ تَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا وَلَٰكِنَّا كُنَّا مُرۡسِلِينَ
28:45.en: But We produced [many] generations [after Moses], and prolonged was their duration. And you were not a resident among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were senders [of this message]

28:46.ar: وَمَا كُنتَ بِجَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ إِذۡ نَادَيۡنَا وَلَٰكِن رَّحۡمَةࣰ مِّن رَّبِّكَ لِتُنذِرَ قَوۡمࣰ ا مَّآ أَتَىٰهُم مِّن نَّذِيرࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
28:46.en: And you were not at the side of the mount when We called [Moses] but [were sent] as a mercy from your Lord to warn a people to whom no warner had come before you that they might be reminded

28:47.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ أَن تُصِيبَهُم مُّصِيبَةُۢ بِمَا قَدَّمَتۡ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ فَيَقُولُواْ رَبَّنَا لَوۡلَآ أَرۡسَلۡتَ إِلَيۡنَا رَسُولࣰ ا فَنَتَّبِعَ ءَايَٰتِكَ وَنَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
28:47.en: And if not that a disaster should strike them for what their hands put forth [of sins] and they would say, "Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses and been among the believers

28:48.ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِنۡ عِندِنَا قَالُواْ لَوۡلَآ أُوتِيَ مِثۡلَ مَآ أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰٓۚ أَوَلَمۡ يَكۡفُرُواْ بِمَآ أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰ مِن قَبۡلُۖ قَالُواْ سِحۡرَانِ تَظَٰهَرَا وَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا بِكُلࣲّ كَٰفِرُونَ
28:48.en: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given like that which was given to Moses?" Did they not disbelieve in that which was given to Moses before? They said, "[They are but] two works of magic supporting each other, and indeed we are, in both, disbelievers

28:49.ar: قُلۡ فَأۡتُواْ بِكِتَٰبࣲ مِّنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ أَهۡدَىٰ مِنۡهُمَآ أَتَّبِعۡهُ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
28:49.en: Say, "Then bring a scripture from Allah which is more guiding than either of them that I may follow it, if you should be truthful

28:50.ar: فَإِن لَّمۡ يَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لَكَ فَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّمَا يَتَّبِعُونَ أَهۡوَآءَهُمۡۚ وَمَنۡ أَضَلُّ مِمَّنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُ بِغَيۡرِ هُدࣰ ى مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
28:50.en: But if they do not respond to you - then know that they only follow their [own] desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people

28:51.en: And We have [repeatedly] conveyed to them the Qur'an that they might be reminded

28:52.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبۡلِهِۦ هُم بِهِۦ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
28:52.en: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they are believers in it

28:53.ar: وَإِذَا يُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡ قَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبۡلِهِۦ مُسۡلِمِينَ
28:53.en: And when it is recited to them, they say, "We have believed in it; indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed we were, [even] before it, Muslims [submitting to Allah]

28:54.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يُؤۡتَوۡنَ أَجۡرَهُم مَّرَّتَيۡنِ بِمَا صَبَرُواْ وَيَدۡرَءُونَ بِٱلۡحَسَنَةِ ٱلسَّيِّئَةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
28:54.en: Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured and [because] they avert evil through good, and from what We have provided them they spend

28:55.ar: وَإِذَا سَمِعُواْ ٱللَّغۡوَ أَعۡرَضُواْ عَنۡهُ وَقَالُواْ لَنَآ أَعۡمَٰلُنَا وَلَكُمۡ أَعۡمَٰلُكُمۡ سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكُمۡ لَا نَبۡتَغِي ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
28:55.en: And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it and say, "For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. Peace will be upon you; we seek not the ignorant

28:56.ar: إِنَّكَ لَا تَهۡدِي مَنۡ أَحۡبَبۡتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِٱلۡمُهۡتَدِينَ
28:56.en: Indeed, [O Muhammad], you do not guide whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided

28:57.ar: وَقَالُوٓاْ إِن نَّتَّبِعِ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ مَعَكَ نُتَخَطَّفۡ مِنۡ أَرۡضِنَآۚ أَوَلَمۡ نُمَكِّن لَّهُمۡ حَرَمًا ءَامِنࣰ ا يُجۡبَىٰٓ إِلَيۡهِ ثَمَرَٰتُ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ رِّزۡقࣰ ا مِّن لَّدُنَّا وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
28:57.en: And they say, "If we were to follow the guidance with you, we would be swept from our land." Have we not established for them a safe sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things as provision from Us? But most of them do not know

28:58.ar: وَكَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا مِن قَرۡيَةِۭ بَطِرَتۡ مَعِيشَتَهَاۖ فَتِلۡكَ مَسَٰكِنُهُمۡ لَمۡ تُسۡكَن مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ اۖ وَكُنَّا نَحۡنُ ٱلۡوَٰرِثِينَ
28:58.en: And how many a city have We destroyed that was insolent in its [way of] living, and those are their dwellings which have not been inhabited after them except briefly. And it is We who were the inheritors

28:59.ar: وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ مُهۡلِكَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡعَثَ فِيٓ أُمِّهَا رَسُولࣰ ا يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِنَاۚ وَمَا كُنَّا مُهۡلِكِي ٱلۡقُرَىٰٓ إِلَّا وَأَهۡلُهَا ظَٰلِمُونَ
28:59.en: And never would your Lord have destroyed the cities until He had sent to their mother a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would not destroy the cities except while their people were wrongdoers

28:60.ar: وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّن شَيۡءࣲ فَمَتَٰعُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَزِينَتُهَاۚ وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيۡرࣱ وَأَبۡقَىٰٓۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
28:60.en: And whatever thing you [people] have been given - it is [only for] the enjoyment of worldly life and its adornment. And what is with Allah is better and more lasting; so will you not use reason

28:61.ar: أَفَمَن وَعَدۡنَٰهُ وَعۡدًا حَسَنࣰ ا فَهُوَ لَٰقِيهِ كَمَن مَّتَّعۡنَٰهُ مَتَٰعَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا ثُمَّ هُوَ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ مِنَ ٱلۡمُحۡضَرِينَ
28:61.en: Then is he whom We have promised a good promise which he will obtain like he for whom We provided enjoyment of worldly life [but] then he is, on the Day of Resurrection, among those presented [for punishment in Hell]

28:68.ar: وَرَبُّكَ يَخۡلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ وَيَخۡتَارُۗ مَا كَانَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُۚ سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
28:68.en: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; not for them was the choice. Exalted is Allah and high above what they associate with Him

28:71.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ سَرۡمَدًا إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ مَنۡ إِلَٰهٌ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ يَأۡتِيكُم بِضِيَآءٍۚ أَفَلَا تَسۡمَعُونَ
28:71.en: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the night continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not hear

28:72.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلنَّهَارَ سَرۡمَدًا إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ مَنۡ إِلَٰهٌ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ يَأۡتِيكُم بِلَيۡلࣲ تَسۡكُنُونَ فِيهِۚ أَفَلَا تُبۡصِرُونَ
28:72.en: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the day continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you a night in which you may rest? Then will you not see

28:73.ar: وَمِن رَّحۡمَتِهِۦ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ لِتَسۡكُنُواْ فِيهِ وَلِتَبۡتَغُواْ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
28:73.en: And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and [by day] seek from His bounty and [that] perhaps you will be grateful

28:76.ar: ۞إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوۡمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكُنُوزِ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُۥ لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلۡعُصۡبَةِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُوَّةِ إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُۥ قَوۡمُهُۥ لَا تَفۡرَحۡۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡفَرِحِينَ
28:76.en: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he tyrannized them. And We gave him of treasures whose keys would burden a band of strong men; thereupon his people said to him, "Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant

28:77.ar: وَٱبۡتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۖ وَلَا تَنسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَأَحۡسِن كَمَآ أَحۡسَنَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيۡكَۖ وَلَا تَبۡغِ ٱلۡفَسَادَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
28:77.en: But seek, through that which Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter; and [yet], do not forget your share of the world. And do good as Allah has done good to you. And desire not corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not like corrupters

28:78.ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمٍ عِندِيٓۚ أَوَلَمۡ يَعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدۡ أَهۡلَكَ مِن قَبۡلِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ مَنۡ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنۡهُ قُوَّةࣰ وَأَكۡثَرُ جَمۡعࣰ اۚ وَلَا يُسۡـَٔلُ عَن ذُنُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ
28:78.en: He said, "I was only given it because of knowledge I have." Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him of generations those who were greater than him in power and greater in accumulation [of wealth]? But the criminals, about their sins, will not be asked

28:79.ar: فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ فِي زِينَتِهِۦۖ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا يَٰلَيۡتَ لَنَا مِثۡلَ مَآ أُوتِيَ قَٰرُونُ إِنَّهُۥ لَذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمࣲ‏
28:79.en: So he came out before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said, "Oh, would that we had like what was given to Qarun. Indeed, he is one of great fortune

28:80.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمَ وَيۡلَكُمۡ ثَوَابُ ٱللَّهِ خَيۡرࣱ لِّمَنۡ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ اۚ وَلَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلصَّٰبِرُونَ
28:80.en: But those who had been given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for he who believes and does righteousness. And none are granted it except the patient

28:81.ar: فَخَسَفۡنَا بِهِۦ وَبِدَارِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ مِن فِئَةࣲ يَنصُرُونَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُنتَصِرِينَ
28:81.en: And We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. And there was for him no company to aid him other than Allah, nor was he of those who [could] defend themselves

28:82.ar: وَأَصۡبَحَ ٱلَّذِينَ تَمَنَّوۡاْ مَكَانَهُۥ بِٱلۡأَمۡسِ يَقُولُونَ وَيۡكَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَقۡدِرُۖ لَوۡلَآ أَن مَّنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا لَخَسَفَ بِنَاۖ وَيۡكَأَنَّهُۥ لَا يُفۡلِحُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ
28:82.en: And those who had wished for his position the previous day began to say, "Oh, how Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it! If not that Allah had conferred favor on us, He would have caused it to swallow us. Oh, how the disbelievers do not succeed

28:83.ar: تِلۡكَ ٱلدَّارُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ نَجۡعَلُهَا لِلَّذِينَ لَا يُرِيدُونَ عُلُوࣰّ ا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا فَسَادࣰ اۚ وَٱلۡعَٰقِبَةُ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ
28:83.en: That home of the Hereafter We assign to those who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth or corruption. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous

28:84.ar: مَن جَآءَ بِٱلۡحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُۥ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡهَاۖ وَمَن جَآءَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ فَلَا يُجۡزَى ٱلَّذِينَ عَمِلُواْ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ إِلَّا مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
28:84.en: Whoever comes [on the Day of Judgement] with a good deed will have better than it; and whoever comes with an evil deed - then those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except [as much as] what they used to do

28:85.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِي فَرَضَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لَرَآدُّكَ إِلَىٰ مَعَادࣲۚ قُل رَّبِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَن جَآءَ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَمَنۡ هُوَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
28:85.en: Indeed, [O Muhammad], He who imposed upon you the Qur'an will take you back to a place of return. Say, "My Lord is most knowing of who brings guidance and who is in clear error

28:86.ar: وَمَا كُنتَ تَرۡجُوٓاْ أَن يُلۡقَىٰٓ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ إِلَّا رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّن رَّبِّكَۖ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ ظَهِيرࣰ ا لِّلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
28:86.en: And you were not expecting that the Book would be conveyed to you, but [it is] a mercy from your Lord. So do not be an assistant to the disbelievers

28:87.ar: وَلَا يَصُدُّنَّكَ عَنۡ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ بَعۡدَ إِذۡ أُنزِلَتۡ إِلَيۡكَۖ وَٱدۡعُ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَۖ وَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
28:87.en: And never let them avert you from the verses of Allah after they have been revealed to you. And invite [people] to your Lord. And never be of those who associate others with Allah

28:88.ar: وَلَا تَدۡعُ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَۘ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۚ كُلُّ شَيۡءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجۡهَهُۥۚ لَهُ ٱلۡحُكۡمُ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
28:88.en: And do not invoke with Allah another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will be destroyed except His Face. His is the judgement, and to Him you will be returned

nH582Q7FoMQ.title: Surat Al-Qasas Summary
nH582Q7FoMQ.one_line: Al-Qasas teaches that our lives are intertwined stories we only see in part: do not judge others, trust Allah, and live your own story well.
nH582Q7FoMQ.summary: After reviewing the previous cluster of surahs on carrying the message, he opens the fifth cluster, which he says is about relationships, and reads Al-Qasas as the surah of stories: how our stories interweave with others' and how what we see is often not what is happening. It is the one place the Quran tells Musa's story nearly whole. He walks through scenes that look wrong from outside: a mother throwing her infant into the river, a tyrant applauded for adopting a foundling who will destroy him, a young man killing someone while defending a friend, a prince fleeing into exile. Each turned out differently than an observer would judge, and Madyan, which Musa saw as his worst day, trained him in patience, responsibility and control of his anger before revelation came. He ties the verse on not being able to guide those you love to the Prophet's grief over Abu Talib, and Qarun to people who envy what they do not understand. His lessons: do not judge others' stories, trust Allah because you cannot control the storyline, and contribute positively wherever your story crosses someone else's.

outline.heading: Review: the cluster on carrying the message
outline.gist: The previous surahs taught that the message passes through families and individuals, needs flexibility and steadfastness, and is shaped by public narratives and power.

outline.heading: A new cluster on relationships; Al-Qasas and our stories
outline.gist: Everything comes down to relationships; this surah is about how our stories intertwine and how we often misread them.

outline.heading: Interlude
The one full telling of Musa's story
outline.gist: Elsewhere the Quran gives snapshots; here the story runs from the river he was thrown into to the sea he crossed.

outline.heading: A mother throws her infant into the river
outline.gist: From outside it looks like madness or abuse; in reality Allah returned him to her as a prince and she nursed him safely.

outline.heading: Pharaoh raises the one who will destroy him
outline.gist: Applauded as a philanthropist while slaughtering children, he reluctantly adopted the boy at Asiyah's urging, never seeing where it would lead.

outline.heading: Musa strikes a man while defending a friend
outline.gist: An onlooker would call him a criminal; it was an accidental killing by a young man who struggled with anger.

outline.heading: Lessons: do not judge, trust Allah, accept complexity
outline.gist: Stories never end neatly and one leads into another; accepting that we cannot grasp or control them brings peace.

outline.heading: Flight from Egypt: the worst day of his life?
outline.gist: A prince turned fugitive, he would have judged his own story as a disaster.

outline.heading: Watering the flocks in Madyan and a marriage offer
outline.gist: He helps two women, is invited by their wise father, and marries for a dowry of eight to ten years of shepherding.

outline.heading: Madyan as training for prophethood
outline.gist: Responsibility, family and the patience of tending animals tempered his anger; revelation came on the way back, which would never have happened had he stayed.

outline.heading: Interlude
Pharaoh's arrogance and drowning
outline.gist: He demanded a tower to look for Musa's God and was thrown into the same river where he found Musa.

outline.heading: You cannot guide those you love
outline.gist: Revealed around Abu Talib's death; stories do not end like films, so do not judge what you do not know.

outline.heading: Worldly decoration versus what is with Allah
outline.gist: What we are given here is adornment; the promise of the Hereafter is far greater.

outline.heading: Allah chooses the storyline; make the best of crossings
outline.gist: We did not choose our story; live it, assume others have struggles we cannot see, and make shared moments good.

outline.heading: Could anyone bring back the day or the night?
outline.gist: We control nothing of our environment; out of mercy He keeps things moving, so trust Him.

outline.heading: Qarun as people saw him
outline.gist: They envied his wealth, not seeing his unhappiness or his coming downfall; he was told to do good as Allah did good to him but credited himself.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Hereafter for those who seek no arrogance; a promised return
outline.gist: The pious win in the end; the grieving Prophet is promised he will be brought back.

outline.heading: You never expected the Book; all perishes but His Face
outline.gist: The Prophet did not write his own story either; every story ends except Allah's.

outline.heading: Our stories are simpler than we think
outline.gist: Qarun's was vanity, Musa's was anger then courage and ethics; live yours well, contribute to others' and do not judge.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Quranic stories
themes.note: Musa's life from the river to Madyan shows how events look different from outside than they really are.

themes.label: Not judging others
themes.note: We see only fragments of others' stories, so judgment is usually wrong; assume people carry struggles we cannot see.

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: We do not choose or control the storyline; trusting Allah while doing what is right is what carried Musa.

themes.label: Anger
themes.note: Musa's anger led to a killing; years of shepherding taught him to control it.

themes.label: Wealth

68:33.en: Such is the punishment [of this world]. And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew

68:34.ar: إِنَّ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ جَنَّٰتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ

68:39.en: Or do you have oaths [binding] upon Us, extending until the Day of Resurrection, that indeed for you is whatever you judge

68:43.en: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. And they used to be invited to prostration while they were sound

z987kuBoK_E.title: Surat Al-Qalam Summary
z987kuBoK_E.one_line: Al-Qalam as the surah of values: the Prophet's great character, the traits to avoid, the owners of the garden, and perseverance under scrutiny.
z987kuBoK_E.summary: Placing Al-Qalam in the juz that teaches dawah, he calls it the surah of ethics and values, revealed very early right after the first verses of Al-Alaq. After the oath by the pen and the praise of the Prophet's great character, the surah teaches by naming who not to be like, which he says leaves more room than a list of what to do. He walks through the traits: refusing clear truth, lying, mocking, gossip, withholding, harshness, selling out principles, and disowning one's roots, which he ties to Muslims raised in the West who confuse integration with losing identity. Flipped, each trait describes the Prophet. The story of the garden owners, who schemed to harvest early so the poor would find nothing, shows that stopping an existing good is worse than never starting, that forgetting Allah is what makes such schemes possible, and that misused blessings lose their barakah. The surah defines a Muslim against a criminal, making Islam an ethical identity, commands perseverance, warns against Yunus's early loss of patience, and describes enemies staring in hope that the Prophet would slip ethically. He asks Muslims to hold to these values because they too are watched.

outline.heading: A juz on dawah; Al-Mulk as its knowledge
outline.gist: Juz 29 teaches how to call to Islam; Al-Mulk set out what one must know: Allah's attributes, our purpose and the consequences.

outline.heading: Al-Qalam: an early surah on values
outline.gist: Revealed right after the first verses of Al-Alaq, it addresses the ethics a Muslim must carry.

outline.heading: By the pen and what they write
outline.gist: Everything we do is recorded, and writing transformed humanity and preserved the Quran.

outline.heading: Not insane, and of great character
outline.gist: Allah honours the Prophet's morals, which is what we follow.

outline.heading: Teaching by who not to be
outline.gist: Telling people what to avoid opens a wide range of permissible paths and is easier to accept than a narrow prescription.

outline.heading: Liars, mockers, gossips, withholders, the harsh
outline.gist: Those who refuse clear truth, lack integrity, spread gossip, hold back aid or are difficult and disrespectful to deal with.

outline.heading: Zanim: disowning one's heritage
outline.gist: Children raised in the West can lose their roots; true integration means knowing who you are and working in harmony with others.

outline.heading: Flip the traits and you find the Prophet
outline.gist: He accepted truth, never lied or mocked, gave freely, was easygoing and proud of his heritage.

outline.heading: Selling out one's principles
outline.gist: Compromising principles for money is not flexibility; the Prophet refused every such offer.

outline.heading: The garden owners: a father's generous tradition
outline.gist: Their father opened the gates to the poor at harvest; stopping an existing good is worse than never starting one.

outline.heading: The joy of giving
outline.gist: Seeing relief in someone's eyes is a joy that takers never know; teach it to your children.

outline.heading: Withholding without wanting the blame
outline.gist: Too cowardly to say it openly, the sons sought their way while avoiding accountability.

outline.heading: The plan to harvest before dawn
outline.gist: The needy would find open gates and nothing left; they set out able and determined to withhold.

outline.heading: The burned garden: did I not tell you?
outline.gist: They thought they were lost until they recognised the ruin; the wisest asks why they did not glorify Allah.

outline.heading: Remembering Allah is what keeps values alive
outline.gist: Belief and ethics are connected; schemes like theirs require switching off the thought of Allah.

outline.heading: Misused blessings lose their barakah
outline.gist: They repented; whatever is treated as exclusively ours is taken away, or its joy and blessing are drained.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Muslim and the criminal
outline.gist: The surah contrasts a Muslim not with a disbeliever but with a mujrim, someone who steals, kills and oppresses.

outline.heading: A Muslim is an ethical being
outline.gist: Once you accept Islam you cannot live without ethics or harm others.

outline.heading: Perseverance as half the religion
outline.gist: Half of life is hardship, and the test is whether our ethics and behaviour hold through it.

outline.heading: Do not be like the man of the whale
outline.gist: Yunus, the first prophet named in revelation, lost patience with his people too early and left without permission.

outline.heading: Staring to make him slip
outline.gist: His enemies watched for any ethical slip, a lie, a scandal or embezzlement, and found none.

outline.heading: With no ethical charge, they called him insane
outline.gist: Insanity is not a moral fault; they used it because none of the surah's vices could be pinned on him.

outline.heading: Every Muslim is watched the same way
outline.gist: Some wait for a single slip to smear a Muslim's name; had the Prophet slipped, none of this would exist.

outline.heading: The most examined life in history
outline.gist: Even a passing thought and a momentary frown at a blind man were corrected in the Quran; learn the surah's values to carry dawah.

outline.heading: Outro

29:23.en: And the ones who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and the meeting with Him - those have despaired of My mercy, and they will have a painful punishment
